record.paper_title: Selection Principles and Special Sets of Reals
record.original_question: Does there exist an analytic topological group that satisfies Sfin(Onbd, O) but fails S1(Ωnbd, Γ)?

evidence.quote: Is there an analytic group satisfying Sfin(Onbd, O) but not S1(Ωnbd, Γ)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a topological group whose underlying topological space is analytic (i.e., a continuous image of the Baire space $\omega^\omega$). Let $\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{nbd}}$ denote the family of covers of $G$ of the form $\{gU : g \in G\}$ where $U$ is a neighborhood of the identity, and let $\mathcal{O}$ denote the family of open covers of $G$. Let $\Omega_{\mathrm{nbd}}$ denote the family of $\omega$-covers consisting of left translates of identity neighborhoods (i.e., covers $\mathcal{U}\subseteq \mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{nbd}}$ such that every finite subset of $G$ is contained in some member of $\mathcal{U}$), and let $\Gamma$ denote the family of $\gamma$-covers (infinite open covers in which every point of $G$ belongs to all but finitely many members).

Recall the selection principles:
\begin{itemize}
\item $S_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})$: for every sequence $(\mathcal{U}_n)_{n\in\omega}$ with $\mathcal{U}_n \in \mathcal{A}$, there exist finite subsets $\mathcal{F}_n \subseteq \mathcal{U}_n$ such that $\bigcup_n \mathcal{F}_n \in \mathcal{B}$.
\item $S_1(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})$: for every sequence $(\mathcal{U}_n)_{n\in\omega}$ with $\mathcal{U}_n \in \mathcal{A}$, there exist $U_n \in \mathcal{U}_n$ such that $\{U_n : n\in\omega\} \in \mathcal{B}$.
\end{itemize}

Question: Does there exist an analytic topological group $G$ that satisfies $S_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{nbd}}, \mathcal{O})$ but does not satisfy $S_1(\Omega_{\mathrm{nbd}}, \Gamma)$?
